title: Status Epilepticus and Acute Seizures: ED Stabilisation

evidenceAudit.scope: Adult convulsive status epilepticus in the emergency department (ED): airway and glucose, benzodiazepine, second-line and refractory therapy, using NICE NG217, the American Epilepsy Society guideline and the Neurocritical Care Society guideline.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-18.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: NICE NG217 section 7 gives timing and drug order but no doses; doses come from the Neurocritical Care Society 2012 and American Epilepsy Society 2016 guidelines.
The Saudi adapted guideline for paediatric convulsive status epilepticus was found but is paediatric and was not used; no Saudi adult guideline was opened.
Pregnancy-specific advice was not found in the opened NG217 section; for eclampsia use the pre-eclampsia pathway.
Thiamine and dextrose doses are not given in the opened sources.
SFDA registration of fosphenytoin, levetiracetam IV, valproate IV and lacosamide was not verified.
Non-convulsive status epilepticus management was not covered in the opened sources.
Source pages were read through automated page extraction rather than page-by-page in the original documents, so each figure should be spot-checked against the source during clinical review.

pathophysiology.summary: Convulsive status epilepticus is seizure activity lasting 5 minutes or more (NG217). Airway, gas exchange, glucose and blood pressure need active management from the first minutes (NCS Table 5). A benzodiazepine is first-line treatment and is repeated once if the seizure continues (NG217, AES). Refractory status epilepticus persists after first- and second-line therapy and needs anaesthetic control under continuous electroencephalogram (EEG) monitoring.

symptoms: Tonic-clonic movements lasting 5 minutes or more.
Repeated seizures without recovery between them.
physicalSigns: Hypoglycaemia, hypoxia or hypotension on first check.
redFlags: No response to two benzodiazepine doses.
Airway or gas exchange compromise, systolic blood pressure below 90 mmHg or mean arterial pressure below 70 mmHg.
Suspected meningitis, encephalitis or raised intracranial pressure.
Pregnancy: treat as eclampsia with magnesium sulfate.
precipitants: Alcohol or drug withdrawal or toxicity.

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Fingerstick glucose at 0–2 minutes; give thiamine before dextrose.
Altered mental state without convulsion; continuous EEG within 1 hour of suspicion.
Pregnancy with severe hypertension; use magnesium sulfate.

clinicalManagement.title: Stabilise
actions: Position the airway, give oxygen, check vital signs and fingerstick glucose at 0–2 minutes; obtain IV access by 5 minutes.
Intubate within 0–10 minutes if the airway or gas exchange is compromised or raised intracranial pressure is suspected.
Give thiamine before dextrose if hypoglycaemic.

clinicalManagement.title: First-line benzodiazepine
actions: IV lorazepam 4 mg (0.1 mg/kg, maximum 4 mg per dose), repeat once in 5–10 minutes; or IM midazolam 10 mg; or IV diazepam 10 mg (0.15 mg/kg), repeat once.
Give an adequate single full dose, not split small doses.
Without IV access: IM midazolam, or buccal or rectal options per local protocol.

clinicalManagement.title: Second-line antiseizure medicine
clinicalManagement.timeframe: From 5–10 minutes after the first benzodiazepine dose (NCS); AES second therapy starts at 20 minutes
actions: If two benzodiazepine doses fail, give levetiracetam, phenytoin or sodium valproate IV; levetiracetam may be quicker and have fewer adverse effects.
Levetiracetam 1,000–3,000 mg IV; valproate 20–40 mg/kg IV; phenytoin 20 mg/kg IV with cardiac monitoring; phenobarbital 20 mg/kg IV if none available.

clinicalManagement.title: Refractory status epilepticus
actions: Seek expert guidance; consider an alternative second-line drug or phenobarbital or general anaesthesia (NG217).
NCS infusions: midazolam bolus 0.2 mg/kg then 0.05–2 mg/kg per hour, or propofol 1–2 mg/kg load then 30–200 µg/kg per minute.
Admit to the intensive care unit (ICU) with continuous EEG; titrate to EEG endpoints.

clinicalManagement.title: Find the cause
actions: Send blood tests, consider head CT, lumbar puncture and toxicology by presentation.
Treat the cause; consider vasopressors if systolic pressure is below 90 mmHg.

medicationPlan.note: NICE NG217 gives the drug order but no doses; doses are from the Neurocritical Care Society 2012 (Table 7, Table 8) and the American Epilepsy Society 2016 guideline. Adult doses only. SFDA registration was not verified; check hospital formulary.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: If seizure has not stopped 5 to 10 minutes after the first dose (NG217).

Advise on driving restrictions according to current Saudi guidance (not verified here).
lifestyleAndDiet: Avoid triggers such as sleep deprivation and alcohol; adhere to antiseizure medicine.

dischargeCriteria: Disposition after status epilepticus is not specified in the opened sources; follow local policy and neurology advice.
